description: C++ programs for ESP8266 development boards such as NodeMCU and ESP-01.

lessons.name: 01 Blink LED
lessons.description: Blink an LED using the ESP8266.
lessons.connectionGuide:
ESP8266 NodeMCU:
Use GPIO 2 (D4) for the LED.

External LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 2 / D4
Cathode (-) -> GND

NodeMCU boards commonly have a built-in LED connected to GPIO 2.

lessons.name: 02 Button Input
lessons.description: Read a push button and control an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> ESP8266 D3 / GPIO 0
Other leg -> GND

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D4 / GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is enabled.

lessons.name: 03 Buzzer
lessons.description: Generate a tone using a buzzer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Buzzer:
Positive (+) -> ESP8266 D6 / GPIO 12
Negative (-) -> GND

The buzzer produces a 1000 Hz tone for 500 milliseconds.

lessons.name: 04 Traffic Light
lessons.description: Control red, yellow, and green LEDs using the ESP8266.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Red LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D5 / GPIO 14
Cathode (-) -> GND

Yellow LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D6 / GPIO 12
Cathode (-) -> GND

Green LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D7 / GPIO 13
Cathode (-) -> GND.

lessons.name: 05 Serial Monitor
lessons.description: Display messages and analog readings in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external components are required.

Connect the ESP8266 to the computer using USB.

Open Arduino IDE -> Tools -> Serial Monitor.
Set the baud rate to 115200.

A0 is used for analog input.

lessons.name: 06 Analog Input
lessons.description: Read an analog value from a potentiometer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Potentiometer:
Connect the potentiometer according to your ESP8266 board's A0 input range.

Middle pin -> A0
Other two pins -> appropriate supply and GND.

IMPORTANT: Check your ESP8266 board's A0 voltage limit before connecting an external voltage.

lessons.name: 07 LED Fade
lessons.description: Fade an LED using ESP8266 PWM.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D5 / GPIO 14
Cathode (-) -> GND

ESP8266 PWM uses a default range of 0 to 1023.

lessons.name: 08 Light Sensor
lessons.description: Read an LDR and automatically control an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LDR circuit:
Use the LDR and a suitable resistor as a voltage divider.

Voltage divider output -> A0

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D4 / GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

Check your ESP8266 board's A0 input voltage limit before connecting the sensor.

lessons.name: 09 Button Counter
lessons.description: Count button presses and display the count in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> ESP8266 D3 / GPIO 0
Other leg -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is used.

Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud to view the counter.

lessons.name: 10 Button LED Toggle
lessons.description: Toggle an LED ON and OFF each time the button is pressed.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> ESP8266 D3 / GPIO 0
Other leg -> GND

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D4 / GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

Each button press toggles the LED between ON and OFF.
